thread:
Priya: Heads up 1: large enterprise (Mercury Health) asked for a turnkey commit plan: reserved GPUs, autoscale rules, pricing tiers, and answers to their security questionnaire. They need this in the SOW by EOW. cc @Ethan @Rae
Ethan: Do we have their traffic profile? steady vs burst, average tokens?
Priya: From the TAM call: steady 400 rps, two daily peaks for care reminders ~1.8k rps for 10-20 minutes, avg prompt ~120 tokens in / 80 tokens out. SLOs: p95 <250ms, p99 <700ms. Multi-AZ preferred but single region.
Rae: Ballpark capacity math: assume 55k output tokens/sec per equivalent A100 for their model mix. With 80 output tokens -> ~687 req/s per GPU ideal, but with KV cache, batching variance and safety, use 375 rps/GPU sustained. For 1.8k peak -> ~5 GPUs, add 50% headroom -> 8 GPUs committed. Recommend committed=6, burst to 12 with autoscale prewarm.
Jordan: Why committed 6 not 8?
Rae: Commit tuned for typical sustained demand plus cost tradeoff. Committed 6 covers baseline+short spikes; burst covers large campaign windows. We can present two pricing options: conservative commit (8) vs lean commit (6 + larger burst).
Priya: Put both options in SOW with cost delta. Also need exact autoscale policy so legal can sign.
Ethan: Example SOW snippet below, ready to paste:
```
capacity_commit:
  option_a:
    committed_gpus: 8
    burst_limit_gpus: 12
    prewarm_minutes: 5
  option_b:
    committed_gpus: 6
    burst_limit_gpus: 16
    prewarm_minutes: 10
autoscale:
  min_active: 3
  scale_unit: gpu
  target_rps_per_gpu: 375
  cooldown_seconds: 600
  burst_policy: credit_based
  az_strategy: active-standby (spread for HA)
fallback:
  on_capacity_exhaust: model_fallback_then_queue
```
Rae: On fallback: priority should be preserve p95 for critical requests. So route to lighter quantized model first, then queue non-critical jobs with graceful 429/Retry-After. Configure route tagging so we can track what fell back for billing/observability.
Priya: Security questionnaire notes: they asked for VPC peering, KMS provider, SOC2 date, audit log retention, and for an HSM option. We can provide dedicated reserved with VPC peering and AWS KMS; HSM available as add-on. Time to provision dedicated once CIDR + peering contacts are provided: 4 business days for standard setup, 2-3 weeks for on-prem/private.
Jordan: Pricing suggestion for sales: committed discount table + burst pricing and overage. Example: 30% off on-demand for committed GPUs, burst charged at on-demand, prewarm run as billable runbook (optional). Add a clause for sustained overage billing if burst > X hours/day for 7-day window.
Ethan: Add network readiness requirement: we need CIDRs and peering contact >=72h before scheduled prewarm test. Also require a final capacity validation test 24h before their campaign. Put these as SOW preconditions.
Priya: Action items: (1) Ethan to create SOW snippet with both commit options + pricing table (2) Rae to attach detailed capacity calc and fallback routing rules (3) Jordan to prepare security Q answers and attach redacted questionnaire.
infra-bot: reserved-commit "mercury-commit-1942007766" queued (suggested committed=6, burst_cap=16) 1: pending network handshake.
Rae: Recommendation: schedule a 60m prewarm test at 80% peak on a staging shard to warm KV caches ~48h before go-live. That should reduce cold-start p99s.
Priya: Good call. I'll include a recommended prewarm run and optional paid runbook in SOW.
Jordan: I'll start the security replies and send over the SOC2 report excerpt.
Priya: Thanks everyone 1. I'll assemble the SOW draft and post back for sign-off before EOW.
